cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Only use when the user explicitly invokes this skill by name.
cards.claim: The rpi skill description disables model auto-triggering so the workflow only runs when the human names it.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line description in SKILL.md frontmatter; no data.
cards.landing: .claude/skills/ frontmatter for phase-heavy skills

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Only the top-level RPI skill is independently discoverable
cards.claim: One discoverable SKILL.md routes to per-phase process.md files kept as plain references (a test asserts no other SKILL.md exists), so the always-loaded surface is one short router and phases load on demand.
cards.evidence_detail: Router table maps 14 requests to create-/iterate- process files; enforced by test-rpi.ts.
cards.landing: Skill layout: one router SKILL.md plus per-phase reference files; a model for splitting CLAUDE.md sections

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Users run each phase in a separate context window by default.
cards.claim: Each phase runs in its own context window by default, with the document carrying state; the user may instead continue in place or after compaction.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as default in SKILL.md and workflow.md; next-step commands say run 'here, after compaction, or in a new session'.
cards.landing: Phase routine in ship plan section 0 (one phase per new chat) - already present

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Save current decisions, user approvals, and unfinished questions in the document before handing off.
cards.claim: Handoff between sessions is a saved document holding decisions, approvals and open questions, and each next command embeds the task directory and chosen flow.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule plus example command lines; the 'fresh-phase-resume' and 'partial-research-resume' tests exercise it.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial (P1): the decisions journal and PR body as the document that carries state

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use the shortest path that gives the user useful review points.
cards.claim: Workflow weight is chosen per task: design discussion for few clear options, PRD then TDD for larger features, TDD alone for fixes and refactors, research only otherwise.
cards.evidence_detail: Four-flow table with fit guidance; no usage data.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a lighter path for small phases versus full path for large ones

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The user can start at any step.
cards.claim: Any phase can be entered directly, and implementation may start from any document that specifies the task well enough, so the pipeline is a menu rather than a fixed gate sequence.
cards.evidence_detail: Flowchart edges allow research to implementation directly; workflow-choice.md note says skip the rest if the document suffices.
cards.landing: Phase routine entry rules

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The RPI framework authors recommend not committing the artifacts.
cards.claim: RPI documents live in .agents/artifacts/<branch-or-slug> and are recommended not to be committed, with a branch-name or slug directory rule and ask-if-ambiguous matching.
cards.evidence_detail: Task-directory selection algorithm: reuse obvious match, ask if several plausible, else branch name or kebab slug; sandbox write block triggers a user question.
cards.landing: Evidence folders: harness commits evidence with sha256 manifests, the opposite choice

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Number new workflow documents using the next available `NN-` prefix in the task directory.
cards.claim: Artifacts are numbered NN-type-description.md with frontmatter carrying type and a repos list of identifier plus sha, so every document is pinned to a commit.
cards.evidence_detail: Template frontmatter in all templates; test-rpi.ts asserts each template has repos with exactly identifier and sha and no legacy single-repo fields.
cards.landing: Plan @ <sha> PR body convention; frontmatter pinning on evidence documents

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Make it shorter, more visual, and easier for a person to digest
cards.claim: After writing any workflow document the agent must re-read the prose and show-me guides and review its own output against them, cutting words and sections that do not earn their place.
cards.evidence_detail: A mandatory self-review step added in the 2026-10-31 'document-review step' commit per the inventory.
cards.landing: Post-write self-edit step for the one-page owner view and decisions journal

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: read the subagent instructions from $SKILLBASE/references/subagents/SUBAGENT_NAME.md
cards.claim: Skills carry a conditional fallback: if no subagent tool exists, or the named agents are missing, the parent reads a mirrored agent file and either follows it inline or pastes it into a generic subagent prompt.
cards.evidence_detail: Two `<important if>` blocks in SKILL.md; the tests 'fallback-without-delegation', 'fallback-with-generic-delegation' and 'nested-delegation' check it on Codex.
cards.landing: Agent definitions that must work when custom agents are not registered; portability of .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: <important if="you do not have an Agent() or Task() or other tool for running subagents">
cards.claim: The `<important if>` conditional-block pattern from improve-claude-md is used inside the shipped skill so situational instructions only bind when their condition holds.
cards.evidence_detail: Two such blocks in SKILL.md; README describes improve-claude-md as rewriting CLAUDE.md with these blocks 'to improve instruction adherence'.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: wrap task-specific invariants in conditional blocks
cards.inventory_ref: (A) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md; repos: skills

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: For a task description with no requested step, start with research questions.
cards.claim: With no step named, the default entry is research questions, and the agent must stop and ask which flow the user wants, waiting for the choice before starting the phase.
cards.evidence_detail: Tested by 'flow-choice': asserts no document is written before the user chooses and that a box-drawing chart is shown.
cards.landing: Phase routine first step: stop-and-ask checkpoint before work

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use box-drawing glyphs, not Mermaid.
cards.claim: Choices shown in chat use a plain-text box-and-line chart rather than Mermaid, because the terminal cannot render Mermaid; Mermaid is kept for documents.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart reference file; test asserts a box-drawing code block and the absence of ```mermaid.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (owner one-page view formatting)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: keep the desired change in the separate request document so research stays objective.
cards.claim: The task is split into a neutral questions file for the researcher and a separate request file holding the desired result, so the research agent never sees what is wanted and cannot bias its findings.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase rule; test 'research-isolation' plants decoy request/PRD files and asserts the research session never opened them.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial design; fresh-context refuters given questions without the claim under test
cards.inventory_ref: (B) QRSPI talk / Humans in the Loop (research prompts returning opinions); repos: skills

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Keep this pass small; the next research session does the full investigation.
cards.claim: The questions phase does only a small locate-and-skim pass, then writes two to seven descriptive questions about what exists, each with a concrete starting pointer such as a package or file.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase step 2-3; examples like 'How does the worker recover queued jobs after a restart?'
cards.landing: Phase 0 / discovery step of each ship-plan phase

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Give each agent a bounded, read-only question
cards.claim: Research fans out to two to six read-only subagents on independent areas in parallel, each asked for paths, line references, test patterns and evidence, and the parent waits for all before synthesising.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 2-4 of create-research; also 'resolve conflicting findings against live code'.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool research fan-out template to save as a reusable workflow

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Distinguish tests read from checks run.
cards.claim: Research documents must separate tests merely read from checks actually executed, and any claim that a check passed needs its command and observed result.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule repeated in create-research and iterate-research.
cards.landing: Reviewer rule: fail-before/pass-after per register id must cite command and observed output

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: A reader should understand the main findings by skimming the headers alone.
cards.claim: Findings headers must assert what is true (e.g. 'Workers restore pending jobs before accepting new work') and sections lead with the finding before citing where it lives.
cards.evidence_detail: Template and process rule; same rule recurs in design discussion, PRD and TDD phases.
cards.landing: Takeaway headers in the one-page owner view, decisions journal and CLAUDE.md sections

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Ask for a research question when neither research input is available.
cards.claim: A research phase refuses to start without either a questions document or a direct question; and a standalone research answer ends without a forced next phase.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 1 of create-research; test 'standalone-research' asserts no forced next step and no questions document.
cards.landing: Phase entry preconditions

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Open questions identify behavior that remains to be traced or understood.
cards.claim: The research template mandates an explicit Open Questions section, a per-component Testing Patterns subsection, and a code-reference list stating whether coverage is exhaustive or key files only.
cards.evidence_detail: Template headings: Research Question, Methodology, Summary, Detailed Findings, Code References, Architecture, Open Questions.
cards.landing: Verified-diagnosis record shape in the knowledge-store design

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: You are a documentarian, not a critic or consultant
cards.claim: Research sub-agents are forbidden to suggest improvements, find bugs, critique or root-cause, only to describe the code as it exists with file:line references, so research output stays objective.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated 'DO NOT' list across locator, analyzer and pattern-finder; analyzer tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash, model sonnet.
cards.landing: .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md prompt: add an explicit no-opinions, file:line-only contract

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't read file contents - Just report locations
cards.claim: The locator agent is a find-only role: no Read tool, grouped output by purpose (implementation, tests, config, types, entry points) with directory counts, run on sonnet.
cards.evidence_detail: Frontmatter tools: Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill; description 'Super Grep/Glob/LS tool - use it if you find yourself desiring one of these tools more than once'.
cards.landing: fixflow-explorer (Haiku file locator): tool allow-list without Read, output grouping, call-it-after-two-greps trigger

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Include tests - Show existing test patterns
cards.claim: A pattern-finder agent returns working code snippets with file:line plus the matching test pattern for each implementation pattern found, without ranking them.
cards.evidence_detail: Output template shows variants (offset vs cursor pagination) and a Testing Patterns block; 'Don't recommend one pattern over another'.
cards.landing: A second custom agent for slice conventions (router-service-repository, outbox kinds) feeding phase plans

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Start with 2-3 well-crafted searches before fetching content
cards.claim: The web researcher agent uses a bounded search budget (2-3 searches, 3-5 pages first), prefers curl on llms.txt and .md/.txt URLs over a fetch tool, and ends with a Gaps or Limitations section.
cards.evidence_detail: Agent body; includes the instruction to avoid browser skills unless the user asks.
cards.landing: Agent for dependency-doc lookups (Expo SDK 52, Railway) with a fixed output shape

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: structure outline > tdd > prd > design discussion > research > original request
cards.claim: Implementers get a fixed document precedence when documents conflict, with the user's latest instruction overriding all of them.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in the agent and in implement-outline; tests 'document-precedence' and 'latest-user-direction' assert the cap value from the outline wins (1000) and a later user cap (2000) wins over it.
cards.landing: Ship plan versus CLAUDE.md versus phase brief precedence rule for agents

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: STOP and think deeply about why the outline can't be followed
cards.claim: On a plan mismatch the implementer must stop and report Expected / Found / Why this matters / How should I proceed, instead of improvising.
cards.evidence_detail: Fixed four-line mismatch report format in the agent file.
cards.landing: Decisions journal entry format for plan deviations in a phase PR

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Read files fully - never use limit/offset parameters
cards.claim: The implementer must read every workflow document and every file in full rather than in chunks, and its progress is recorded in the outline itself (checkboxes and a checkmark on the phase heading).
cards.evidence_detail: Getting Started and Progress Tracking sections; model: inherit, tools include Edit/Write/TodoWrite.
cards.landing: Progress marks in the plan file as a self-reported-compliance record; read-in-full rule for phase brief

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: do not mark phase title with ✅ until the human confirms manual verification passed
cards.claim: Automated and manual verification are separate checklists; a phase is marked complete only after automated checks pass and any manual checks are human-confirmed, and the agent pauses for the human when manual checks remain.
cards.evidence_detail: Pause message template; tests 'phase-pause-and-resume' and 'automated-only-phases' assert phase 2 does not run before review and that unconfirmed manual checks never get a checkmark.
cards.landing: Phase closing message / owner view: split automated from human-confirmed items

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Fix failed checks before marking them passed.
cards.claim: The parent re-reviews the implementer's verification evidence and only the parent ticks validation boxes; by default one phase is delegated at a time, and the user can request a group or all phases run continuously.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 2-3 of implement-outline: launch the implementer with a short prompt of paths, precedence and scope, and let it read the documents itself.
cards.landing: Orchestrator-implementer split with a short delegation prompt (paths plus precedence, not pasted content)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Prefer small end-to-end results that cross the relevant module or service boundaries.
cards.claim: The outline is split into vertical slices, each working and verifiable when it ends (serve a simple result, then add editing, then an error path), rather than horizontal layers.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 4; each phase has result, Change Outline and Validation with Automated vs Manual split; Implementation Overview checklist kept in sync.
cards.landing: Ship-plan phase sizing rule (vertical slice per phase with its own checks)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Describe intent and code shape at the level needed to review the work.
cards.claim: The outline carries file trees, contracts, signatures and pseudocode rather than full code, and the implementer's agent states 'outlines describe intent and signatures' - the plan is a reviewable shape, not the implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Outline process plus implementer 'Implementation Philosophy'.
cards.landing: Ship-plan phase specs: contract and signature level, with checks listed per phase
cards.inventory_ref: (B) QRSPI talk (outline as reviewable artifact); repos: skills

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Present one decision at a time with its options and recommendation, then wait
cards.claim: Design is a one-question-at-a-time interview in the main conversation, with options, tradeoffs and a codebase-grounded recommendation; settled choices move into a Resolved Design Questions section with the rejected alternatives and why.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 5; tests 'fresh-design-decision', 'design-with-settled-choices' check settled choices land in Resolved and open ones stay in Design Questions.
cards.landing: Decisions journal format: decision, rationale, alternatives set aside

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Keep this opening short so the interview starts promptly.
cards.claim: A PRD starts as a tiny skeleton (problem drafted, other sections empty), then problem, then success measure, then solution are settled in order, with technical questions parked under Deferred to TDD; the user reads Solution Details whole and approves it.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 2-5; a measure may be recorded as 'none useful' for small work with the user's agreement.
cards.landing: Success measure per phase in the ship plan; deferred-decision list

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: with a separate user approval for each.
cards.claim: The technical design is split into System Design (components, contracts, sequences) approved first, then Program Design (call trees, signatures, file-tree changes, test seams) approved separately; a test asserts the second approval is not skipped or the first restarted.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 3-6; tests 'tdd-interview' and 'fresh-program-design' require at least two approvals and no restart of approved System Design.
cards.landing: Two-gate review (architecture then code shape) before implementation for high-risk phases (money, outbox, lifecycle)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Document patterns to follow with source paths and short examples.
cards.claim: Design documents carry a Patterns to Follow section with source paths and short examples including test seams, so the implementing session copies existing conventions.
cards.evidence_detail: Present in the TDD template and design discussion; the pattern-finder agent feeds it.
cards.landing: Move per-slice conventions out of CLAUDE.md into per-phase Patterns to Follow lists

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Reproduce the issue or check the requested change against code and tests.
cards.claim: Feedback handling is reproduce first, ask one targeted question with a recommended approach if behaviour is unclear, add a regression test, and update outline sections whose agreed result changed.
cards.evidence_detail: Five short steps; tests 'implementation-feedback' and 'finished-iteration-needs-feedback' (a finished doc without feedback prompts for it instead of editing).
cards.landing: Refuter/reviewer fail-before/pass-after requirement for each register id

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't say "it", "that", and similar words unless the referent is obvious.
cards.claim: A shared prose reference imposes Orwell's six rules, direct-answer-first brevity, real names for things instead of invented labels, and no unclear pronoun referents, for responses, docs, commit messages and PR descriptions.
cards.evidence_detail: Short file added Oct 31; loaded after each document is written.
cards.landing: Writing rules for closing message, PR body and decisions journal; a skill loaded on write

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear.
cards.claim: Explain with the smallest suitable visual (pseudocode, call tree, component tree, shallow file tree, Mermaid, diff) and show change as a diff block rather than prose, using a full block only when most is new.
cards.evidence_detail: Catalogue of six view types with examples; ends with 'don't overwhelm the user'.
cards.landing: Reviewer and owner-view format: diff or call-tree instead of narrative

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: write one focused HTML file
cards.claim: For dense UI or concept comparisons the agent writes one focused HTML file (diagram, infographic or short deck) in the product's own palette with real labels and opens it, and saves mockups beside the document as ordinary local links.
cards.evidence_detail: Last bullet of show-me; PRD and design phases save mockup-*.html; test 'local-visuals' asserts the project palette hex appears in the mockup.
cards.landing: Owner one-page view as HTML artifact

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Only the top-level RPI skill is independently discoverable
cards.claim: A static lint test checks the skill itself: every phase named in SKILL.md has a process with numbered steps and a final-answer reference, every $SKILLBASE link resolves, agent copies are byte-identical, and forbidden tokens (Linear, Jira, .humanlayer/) never appear.
cards.evidence_detail: Bun script of assert calls; prints 'RPI checks passed: N phases, N agents, N document templates'.
cards.landing: A cheap structural test for .claude/skills and agents (links resolve, frontmatter valid, mirrored copies equal) in CI

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Test fixtures and transcripts:
cards.claim: A behavioural suite of about 58 named scenarios drives a real agent (codex exec, medium reasoning effort) over throwaway git fixtures, with a 10-minute kill timeout, and asserts on artifacts, git state and the raw tool-call transcripts rather than on the reply wording alone.
cards.evidence_detail: Scenarios include flow-choice, research-isolation, phase-pause-and-resume, document-precedence, fallback and nested-delegation; results.json per run; no pass rates published in the repo.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial as the first of a scripted scenario suite for the phase routine; run at medium effort

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Workflow committed without a user request
cards.claim: Every scenario turn asserts that git HEAD did not move, that implementation code was untouched in document phases, and that no editor was opened unasked: compliance is checked from side effects, not from what the agent says.
cards.evidence_detail: Assertions in turn(), 'questions-handoff' (git diff -- src empty; no code/cursor/open command in events).
cards.landing: Observable-effect compliance checks for the routine in place of self-report (git diff and transcript greps)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Research opened unrelated task documents
cards.claim: The suite plants decoy documents (a DECOY request and PRD contradicting the code) and asserts the session's transcript never opened them, testing that a phase reads only what it is allowed to.
cards.evidence_detail: 'research-isolation' greps the JSON transcript for cat commands and for '# DECOY' in outputs.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial: plant decoy facts in unrelated docs and check the fresh agent does not use them

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Default implementation ran phase 2 before review
cards.claim: The suite tests pause behaviour: by default only phase 1 is implemented and phase 2 code must not exist until manual checks are confirmed, while 'run all phases' completes all and ticks all automated boxes.
cards.evidence_detail: 'phase-pause-and-resume', 'all-phases', 'automated-only-phases'; asserts on retryDelay(9) values and on checkbox text in the saved outline.
cards.landing: A test that the one-phase-per-session rule holds (no next-phase work in the PR)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Internal phases were discovered as broken installed skills
cards.claim: The suite checks stderr for skill-loading failures and tests the skill both installed (symlinked into .agents/skills) and loaded by explicit path, and tests the sub-agent path with and without a delegation tool enabled.
cards.evidence_detail: turn() asserts stderr lacks 'failed to load skill'; scenarios 'explicit-skill-loading', 'fallback-without-delegation', 'nested-delegation' read the session's raw function-call list for spawn_agent.
cards.landing: Verify skills load and subagents are actually spawned by reading the transcript tool-call list

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Host-specific invocation in
cards.claim: Single-source-of-truth tooling: a sync script copies agents and create-/iterate- templates into mirrored reference paths and a --check mode (for CI) fails if any copy drifts or any template hard-codes a host-specific /rpi command instead of <rpi-invocation>.
cards.evidence_detail: Writes 'N RPI reference copies synced/verified'; templates normalised by replacing '/rpi ' with '<rpi-invocation> '.
cards.landing: Drift check between .claude/agents and any mirrored skill reference; a --check step in CI for duplicated prose docs

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Each phase works in a fresh session by default.
cards.claim: The rpi skill is packaged for install via npx skills add and is host-portable: Codex uses $rpi and needs write access granted to the artifacts directory, with a blocked write triggering a user question.
cards.evidence_detail: README product copy for the skill; portability across Claude Code and Codex reflected in test harness using codex exec.
cards.landing: Skill packaging (marketplace.json plus plugin.json listing agents) as the reusable-workflow library format

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Rewrites your CLAUDE.md using `<important if>` blocks to improve instruction adherence.
cards.claim: improve-claude-md is a skill that rewrites a CLAUDE.md with conditional blocks, and the catalogue also lists build-iterated-agentic-loop, design-control-loop (sensor, controller, actuator, disturbances) and narrow-react-prop-types as shipped skills.
cards.evidence_detail: One-paragraph catalogue entries; no adherence numbers in this repo.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim; scheduled agentic loop skill; control-loop framing for verifiers
cards.inventory_ref: (A) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md; repos: skills (design-control-loop by Kyle)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use artifact filenames to locate the current phase when asked what's next
cards.claim: A what's-next query is answered from the filesystem state: artifact filenames identify the phase, and the latest document is read for unfinished work and settled choices, with the newest document chosen when several match and the chosen file named.
cards.evidence_detail: SKILL.md rule; tests 'whats-next', 'whats-next-draft', 'newest-document'.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial: recover phase and facts from repository state alone

gaps: test-rpi-workflows.ts (49KB): fully read only the first ~14KB (helpers, fixtures, first scenarios); the remaining ~50 scenarios were covered via the list of test names and extracted assertion lines, not line-by-line.

Most iterate-*/process.md files (design-discussion, prd, tdd, structure-outline, research-questions) and small *_final_answer.md templates were not read line by line; they are mirrors of the create-* phases by the sync script and sampled via iterate-research and iterate-implementation.
No measured pass rates, costs or adherence numbers exist in the repo; all cards are asserted or marketing.
Per-file commit dates not available from the working copy; all dated to the v1.1.0 release 2026-11-01.
Inventory section letters in inventory_ref are approximate; I matched on the repos/skills commit lines rather than a labelled section.
